knowledge:
- key_parameters: bam_file=Path to the BAM file for coverage calculation ;; vcf_file=Path to the VCF file containing heterozygous SNVs ;; target_chr=The target chromosome to analyze (e.g., "chr21") ;; md=GRanges object containing bin coverage and GC content metadata ;; model=The model to fit, such as "all", "normal", "trisomy", "monosomy", "mosaic trisomy", or "mosaic monosomy" ;; steps=Number of MCMC iterations for posterior distribution estimation
- alternatives: MADloy (specifically optimized for detecting loss of Y chromosome) ;; MoChA (for mosaic chromosomal alterations from WGS/WES) ;; PennCNV (for microarray-based mosaicism detection)
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing high-depth next-generation sequencing data (WGS or WES) to detect and precisely quantify the fraction of cells carrying mosaic chromosomal aneuploidies.
- pitfalls: Low sequencing depth (less than 30x) significantly reduces the accuracy of mosaic fraction estimation. Constitutional copy number variants (CNVs) can be misclassified as mosaic aneuploidies if not pre-filtered. Mismatched reference genomes for GC content correction will lead to false positives.

workflows.name: mosaic_aneuploidy_detection
workflows.intent: Detect, classify, and quantify mosaic aneuploidy from BAM and VCF files using a Bayesian framework.
input: sample.vcf (variant call file for B-allele frequency calculation)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare coverage bins using prepareCoverageBin ;; 2. Run the mosaic aneuploidy detection model using runMadSeq ;; 3. Plot the posterior distribution of the mosaic fraction using plotFraction ;; 4. Plot the coverage and BAF data with the model fit using plotMadSeq
workflows.code:
md <- prepareCoverageBin(bam_file = "sample.bam", bin_size = 100000, genome = "hg19")
res <- runMadSeq(bam_file = "sample.bam", vcf_file = "sample.vcf", target_chr = "chr21", md = md, model = "all", steps = 10000)
plotFraction(res)
plotMadSeq(res)
